item.title: 26 Years Later, BioWare’s Most Influential RPG Is Still Shaping My Life
item.dc:creator: Francesco Cacciatore
item.category: Baldur's Gate II: Shadows of Amn
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgic retrospective about old game, not a new announcement.] BioWare may be gone, but the studio's best RPG, Baldur's Gate 2, built a legacy that is still shaping lives today.
item.content:encoded: The game was Baldur’s Gate 2: Shadows of Amn. The T-shirt, which came with the collector’s edition, sported the game’s logo: two mirrored heads, one in light, one in darkness (the exact meaning of the image has been debated for the past 26 years, with no conclusive answer). I was the kid, of course. Soon after, I bought the game and, for the first time, immersed myself in the world of the Forgotten Realms, brought to life in digital form by BioWare. Almost three decades later, BioWare is gone. The sad news made me reflect on how Baldur’s Gate 2 and the other computer RPGs they developed between the 1990s and the early 2000s marked the trajectory of my life.

item.title: Legendary Sci-Fi Director's 129-Minute War-Action Masterpiece Is Being Cut From Netflix
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: streaming clickbait headline] Starship Troopers, directed by Paul Verhoeven, is a satirical military thriller that lampoons right-wing militarism.
item.content:encoded: When legendary director Paul Verhoeven's space action epic arrived in theaters 29 years ago, a lot of people didn’t get it. While the original 1959 novel by Robert A. Heinlein had a militaristic right-wing viewpoint, Verhoeven and screenwriter Edward Neumeier sought to lampoon those themes when they adapted it for the screen in 1997. Unfortunately, a number of critics mistook the movie’s satire for sincerity. The Washington Post, for example, called the movie “Nazi to the core.”

item.title: 5 Funniest 'Peanuts' Comics About Snoopy's Forgotten Siblings
item.dc:creator: Thomas Hindmarch
item.description: [Filtered: Graphic novel/comic excerpt and nostalgia retrospective filler.] Your Beagle Has a Rich Family Life, Charlie Brown
item.content:encoded: Charles Schulz's Snoopy is one of the most famous fictional dogs in the world, if not the most famous. His only real competition might be Goofy, who's apparently supposed to be an anthropomorphic dog (which, as ever, raises some real uncomfortable questions about Pluto), or possibly Scooby-Doo.

item.title: 29 Years Ago, ‘Buffy’s Wisest Character Got a Shocking Backstory that Redefined the Entire Series
item.dc:creator: Maria Loreto
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old Buffy episode from 29 years ago.] Buffy the Vampire Slayer began to find its rhythm in season 2, after introducing an unnerving backstory to Rupert Giles.
item.content:encoded: In Buffy the Vampire Slayer, Halloween is the one night a year when monsters think it’s cliché to go out and torment the Hellmouth. As Buffy elegantly puts it: Halloween is “like, dead for the undead.” But 29 years ago, one evildoer decided to wreak havoc in Sunnydale on the one night no one expected. The result was an episode that explored the characters' deepest insecurities and gave the Scooby Gang an unexpected hero: Rupert Giles (Anthony Head), the fussy librarian who until then had served as Buffy’s moral compass and cheerleader. While he ended up saving the day, the episode added a wrinkle to his character, introducing his mysterious past as "Ripper."

item.title: The MCU's Oldest Villain Just Made a Surprise Return in 'VisionQuest'
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Marvel franchise casting/character gossip, big-franchise churn filler.] VisionQuest just brought back the character of Raza, the Ten Rings terrorist not seen since the first Iron Man movie
item.content:encoded: In the 2008 movie Iron Man, the biggest, baddest villain was Obadiah Stane, played by Jeff Bridges. Originally business partners with Tony Stark (Robert Downey Jr.), Obadiah betrayed Tony by hatching a plot to kill him while he was in Afghanistan. When Tony survived and became Iron Man, Obadiah responded by taking on his own iron identity: The Iron Monger.

item.title: 5 Adult Fairy Tale Books That Are Magical From Start to Finish
item.dc:creator: Sam Nelson
item.description: [Filtered: Book promotion and graphic novel content outside gaming focus.] Dive into fantastical worlds filled with wizards, fae, and dangerous quests
item.content:encoded: Fairy tales are often the first stories kids learn from picture books, and the works of Hanna Diyab, the Brothers Grimm, and Hans Christian Andersen can help inspire a lifelong passion for reading. But just because you grow up, doesn’t mean you have to abandon the genre. Modern fantasy books often strive for epic scale and complex political scheming, but it can be just as satisfying to explore a wondrous world where brave heroes fall in love and find the courage to do what’s right. If you want to bring some more magic to your reading list, check out these five fairy tale novels for adults.

item.title: How to unlock Lid's second limit burst in Final Fantasy Resonance
item.dc:creator: Josh Broadwell
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Unlocking Lid's second limit burst in Final Fantasy Resonance works differently than the others. Here's how to get Lid's second limit burst
item.content:encoded: Getting Lid's second limit burst in Final Fantasy Resonance works a bit differently than the process of acquiring other characters' bursts. With most of the party, you just level them up, and they unlock once you hit the right milestone. You can guess when that is just from a quick scan of their skill list, as a new skill usually accompanies their new limit burst at the same level. But Lid's skill list is shorter, and since the game doesn't tell you how to unlock her second burst, you might wonder whether you've missed something.

item.title: Pokémon Center Opens More Baffling 30th Anniversary TCG Orders
item.dc:creator: Patricia Hernandez
item.description: [Filtered: Pokémon TCG retail/restock news; trading card scalper adjacent.] Pokémon fans were looking forward to pre-orders for 30th Anniversary UPCs or Battle Decks, but TPC has other TCG plans
item.content:encoded: Pokémon's Eevee-themed 30th Anniversary Battle Deck is scheduled to drop on Oct. 30. A week after that is the release date for the highly-awaited Pokémon 30th Anniversary Ultra Premium Collection, the most expansive (and expensive) product in the celebratory lineup. Is The Pokémon Center doing pre-orders for either of these things this Tuesday? Of course not. The official pocket monster storefront is currently selling new trading card game items from the 30th Anniversary repertoire, yes, but its selection is as random as it is baffling.

item.title: 22 Years Ago, TV’s Best Sci-Fi Show Proved It Was About More Than the Mystery
item.dc:creator: Terry Terrones
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old TV show from 22 years ago.] Lost's "House of the Rising Sun" captures the emotional revelations and tantalizing mysteries that made the series so addictive in 2004.
item.content:encoded: There was a time when Lost was more than just a television show. It was an obsession. Every episode introduced new mysteries, every character seemed to be hiding something, and every Wednesday night left viewers with more questions than answers. In the fall of 2004, nobody knew what was happening on the Island, and that was a huge part of the fun.

item.title: 10 Years Ago, Anime's Most Bonkers Series Introduced a Disturbing Villain Who Changed Everything
item.dc:creator: Debopriyaa Dutta
item.description: [Filtered: Anime nostalgia retrospective, not video game content.] This man has been single-handedly terrorizing Morioh for more than a decade.
item.content:encoded: Part 4 of JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure, called Diamond Is Unbreakable, also features an idyllic town with a rotten core. Author Hirohiko Araki changes things up after a globe-trotting adventure in Stardust Crusaders (Part 3), shifting the scene to the beautiful town of Morioh. Part 3 protagonist Jotaro Kujo seeks out Morioh resident Josuke Higashikata seeking to learn more about his true parentage, which triggers a string of bizarre events in this seemingly peaceful small town.

item.title: Wildwood channels The Decemberists' folk fairytale legacy
item.dc:creator: Matt Patches
item.description: [Filtered: Animation film feature without game connection or real substance.] Colin Meloy and Carson Ellis talk about Laika's movie, the original book, sequels, and Portland.
item.content:encoded: “I feel like when we were first coming up with the story, we were trying to really go for the early stuff — pull from folktale and fair ytale tropes,” Meloy tells Polygon. “I think there’s so many things in the movie that, because that was really the intent from the outset, was to create a fairy tale. Inevitably, it ends up like fantasy in the context of 2026, but that’s what we were shooting for.”

item.title: 8 Most Entertaining Sci-Fi Books of the 21st Century That Are Impossible to Put Down
item.dc:creator: Sam Nelson
item.description: [Filtered: Graphic novel excerpts and book promos are not kept.] Get some laughs with psychic cats, friendly aliens, and snarky cyborgs
item.content:encoded: Science fiction writers imagine humanity's future in order to explore our present and past. The best sci-fi is a mix of cautionary tale and social commentary, but books about heady topics like artificial intelligence, alien encounters, and galaxy-spanning wars are often filled with dense explanations of theoretical technologies or complex political factions. It doesn't have to be that way. While dry and heavy sci-fi can be extremely rewarding to read, the genre also offers plenty of lighter options filled with humor and adventure. If you want some laughs in your future, check out these eight extremely fun sci-fi books that grapple with modern issues facing humanity in the 21st Century.

item.title: Major 'Avatar: Seven Havens’ Korra Reveal May Be Hiding the Truth About the Cataclysm
item.dc:creator: Corey Plante
item.description: [Filtered: Generic animated series news; Avatar falls under big-franchise churn.] Did Korra destroy the world? An Avatar: Seven Havens flashback reveals her attacking Republic City, but the truth may be more complicated.
item.content:encoded: For more than two centuries, the world of Avatar: Seven Havens has remembered Korra as the Avatar who destroyed everything. Everybody from Ellora to New Ba Sing Se has grown up hearing that story, and episode 7 seemingly gives Pavi (Saheli Khan) and Nisha (Aishu Devan) them proof: They witness their predecessor in the Avatar State, tearing apart Republic City as spiritual energy whips through its burning streets.

The protagonist is Soul, a powerful member of the Order who has only 66 days to find a new heart. As he travels, Soul learns about a complex network of conspiracies.

item.title: 24 Years Later, Nintendo's Most Divisive Mario Game Is a Miracle on Switch 2
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Colantonio
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective; old game suddenly popular again pattern.] Super Mario Sunshine was beloved at launch but grew to become one of the most divisive Mario games ever. Here's why it's worth playing in 2026.
item.content:encoded: I can’t remember what I had for lunch yesterday, but I still remember the daySuper Mario Sunshine launched in 2002. It was a summer's day and I couldn’t wait to line up at the GameStop in the Natick Mall to pick up my pre-ordered copy. It was getting rave reviews — a 9.4 from IGN, a 9.75 from Game Informer, perfect marks from Nintendo Power! — so it felt like an instant classic. Players at the time seemed to agree, considering that the 3D platformer would go on to become the third best-selling GameCube game of all time. Everyone loved Super Mario Sunshine.

item.content:encoded: While KPop Demon Hunters fans patiently wait for the forthcoming sequel, Netflix is dropping new video content from 2025's breakout animated musical adventure, starting with footage that didn't appear in the film. On Monday, Netflix released a short video that reveals the full choreography for Huntr/x's "How It's Done," promising that the new clip "is just the opening act" for new KPop Demon Hunters reveals.

item.title: 19 Years Later, a Perfect Avatar Episode Redefined the Show's Greatest Rivalry
item.dc:creator: Sam Nelson
item.description: [Filtered: Generic nostalgia retrospective piece about old episode analysis.] Aang wasn’t the only one with the power to save the world
item.content:encoded: The season 3 episode “The Avatar and the Fire Lord” tells the same story from two perspectives. Avatar Roku (James Garrett) reaches out to Aang through the spirit world to tell him about his own life and death in the Fire Nation while Prince Zuko (Dante Basco) follows a mysterious message to learn the secret history of his great-grandfather, Fire Lord Sozin (Ron Perlman). The episode, which was written by Elizabeth Welch and directed by Ethan Spaulding, shows both Roku and Sozin in a new light.

item.title: 10 Best 'Game of Thrones' Episodes of All Time, Ranked According to Their IMDb Scores
item.dc:creator: Aimee Hart
item.description: [Filtered: Game of Thrones ranking list; Steven already keeps substantive GoT news.] Showrunners David Benioff and D. B. Weiss made 'Game of Thrones' history with these phenomenal 10 episodes.
item.content:encoded: Showrunners David Benioff and D. B. Weiss faced an impossible task: bringing one of the greatest dark fantasy epics ever written — George R.R. Martin’s A Song of Ice and Fire — to television. We all have opinions on how well they succeeded, especially with the ending, but there’s no denying Benioff and Weiss produced some masterful episodes along the way.

item.title: Anne Hathaway’s A24 Box Office Flop Finds Redemption on Streaming
item.dc:creator: Sam Hill
item.description: [Filtered: Streaming clickbait about box office flop finding audience.] Anne Hathaway’s Mother Mary struggled theatrically, but the A24 film is finding a new audience on streaming after its 2026 release.
item.content:encoded: Anne Hathaway is having an absolutely killer 2026. She returned to fashion’s most cutthroat workplace alongside Meryl Streep in The Devil Wears Prada 2, starred in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, went into erotic thriller territory with Verity, and led the dinosaur thriller The End of Oak Street. It’s a blockbuster-heavy lineup for one of Hollywood’s all-time great leading women.

item.title: How to open the sealed stone in Final Fantasy Resonance
item.dc:creator: Josh Broadwell
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Final Fantasy Resonance's sealed stone houses a powerful ally, but the game tells you nothing about how to open it
item.content:encoded: You'll probably run into Final Fantasy Resonance's sealed stone early in your adventure, depending on how far off the beaten path you explore. A really useful prize is waiting inside said stone, too. However, you can't do anything about it for quite some time. It's for the best, really, as you have to fight for that prize, and it's a pretty challenging battle.

item.title: Avatar: Seven Havens Officially Recasts Korra’s Voice
item.dc:creator: Willa Rowe
item.description: [Filtered: Generic TV/animated series casting news; matches past TOSS pattern.] Avatar: Seven Havens' latest episodes revealed who will be voicing Korra in the series
item.content:encoded: One of the most important characters inAvatar: Seven Havens is Korra, even if she's long dead by the time the show starts. The post-apocalyptic world of Seven Havens is directly caused by Korra's actions; at least that is what the show has indicated so far, resulting in widespread hatred toward the Avatar. This is causing a lot of problems for Nisha and Pavi, our new Avatar twins. The most recent batch of episodes brought us even closer to Korra once again and also revealed who provides her voice in Seven Havens.

item.title: FBI Is Officially Investigating An Unprecedented Pokémon Card Heist
item.dc:creator: Patricia Hernandez
item.description: [Filtered: Pokémon TCG retail/heist story; matches past TOSS profile.] The disappearance of over 6,450 cards on a FedEx truck might make this the biggest Pokémon TCG theft of all time
item.content:encoded: Earlier in October, authorities revealed that a FedEx truck reportedly containing nearly $1 million in cards graded by the Professional Sports Authenticator had suddenly gone missing. A couple of weeks later, the apparent theft of 6,451 slabs — many of which contained Pokémon cards — is being scrutinized by the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

item.title: 27 Years Ago, 'Buffy the Vampire' Unleashed an Impossibly Good Season, and Broke the Fandom
item.dc:creator: Jake Kleinman
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old TV show, despite horror tag.] Buffy Season 3 is the best Halloween binge watch with thrilling villains and unforgettable moments.
item.content:encoded: Buffy the Vampire Slayer was no exception. The show's first season was mixed at best, as the cast and writers all struggled to find their footing. Yet Buffy season 2 easily has one of the finest batches of episodes in television history, largely thanks to the introduction of iconic vampire baddies Spike (James Marsters) and Druscilla (Juliet Landau), along with Angel's (David Boreanaz) transformation into the villainous bloodsucker Angelus.

These thousands of avid readers are anticipating Amazon's adaptation of their favorite romantasy series. As more details come out, it's clear that it is close to leaving pre-production. Recent reports provide details about its filming window and location, allowing fans to speculate about the real-world location that will become Navarre and Basgiath War College.

item.title: 27 Years Later, the Best Action Adventure Movie of 1999 Is Officially Free on Youtube
item.dc:creator: Maria Loreto
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: streaming clickbait headline] Brendan Fraser’s best ‘90s blockbuster had a secret ingredient two reboots couldn’t copy
item.content:encoded: No one really knows why a movie works. After a century of Hollywood, the industry is still trying to understand and adapt to an ever-evolving audience. As we enter an era of peak remake and IP-grab filmmaking, stories from decades ago have become the studios’ easiest bets to make money. It’s not fertile ground for creativity, but we movie fans have to take our wins where we can.

item.title: Sydney Sweeney's New Netflix Sci-Fi Space Epic Gets First Details
item.description: [Filtered: Big-franchise churn: Gundam anime adaptation casting gossip.] Netflix's live-action Gundam adaptation stars Sydney Sweeney and Noah Centineo in a Shakespearian action romance space movie epic.
item.content:encoded: The live-action Gundam film has been in the works in some form or another since 2018. A director and cast have been announced, including high-profile names like Sydney Sweeney joining the project. Still, hard details on exactly what Netflix's live-action adaptation of the legendary mech anime series will look like have been almost non-existent.

item.title: 15 Years Later, Batman: Arkham City Remains Batman's Last Gaming Masterpiece
item.dc:creator: Austin Manchester
item.category: LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old game from 15 years ago.] Batman: Arkham City set a new highwater mark for superhero games and has influenced their design and mechanics in the 15 years since its release.
item.content:encoded: Batman: Arkham Asylum was released in 2009 at a time when superhero video games were usually relegated to being uninspired movie tie-ins. Some of them were good, like X-Men Origins: Wolverine, but most of them were either forgettable or downright bad. Arkham Asylum was something different — a superhero game based on an original idea from a renowned Batman writer, Paul Dini (Batman: The Animated Series). It was great, and set the foundation for its even greater 2011 follow-up.

item.title: 6 Hilarious 'Calvin and Hobbes' Comics Where Calvin is a Weird Little Genius
item.dc:creator: Thomas Hindmarch
item.description: [Filtered: Generic comics/graphic novel excerpt; not gaming or horror.] Words and verbs and adjectives, painted up like a picture in these iconic Calvin and Hobbes comic strips
item.content:encoded: Calvin and Hobbes came along at just the right time to influence a generation of creators, many of whom would go on to create comic strips of their own. Alongside a couple of other seminal '90s newspaper comics like Bloom County/Outland, C&H's linework, flexibility, and imagination visibly inspired many of the artists who worked in the 2000s webcomics boom.

item.title: Clayface Gives Skydance Its Second Box Office Weekend Win In A Row
item.dc:creator: Tomas Franzese
item.description: [Filtered: DC franchise box office churn; not prestige/genuinely anticipated] Clayface held off You Can See Everything to top the box office this weekend
item.content:encoded: Initial estimates for Clayface's opening weekend box office are in, and the lower-budget horror film took the top spot with a $24.5 million gross. Its success means Skydance, the company created when Paramount and Warner Bros. merged, has topped the box office for two straight weeks.

item.title: GTA: San Andreas’ Most Frustrating MIssion Show How Far Rockstar Has Come in 22 Years
item.dc:creator: Paulo Kawanishi
item.category: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas – The Definitive Edition
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old game from 22 years ago] Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is a classic game with interesting missions, but its annoying controls just feel worse after 22 years.
item.content:encoded: With the imminent release of Grand Theft Auto 6, I decided it was time to revisit what was probably the biggest game of my childhood: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. In 2005, GTA: San Andreas was one of the first four games I bought for the PlayStation 2, alongside Final Fantasy X, Kingdom Hearts, and Devil May Cry 3. Since I can no longer enjoy that version of the game I played so many times as a kid, I picked up the Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy — Definitive Edition, which includes San Andreas, on Steam and booted up the game.

item.title: 9 Near-Perfect 'Far Side' Comics Starring the Nerdy Kid
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Comic retrospective, not games or Steven's stated interests.] Gary Larson's The Far Side didn't really have recurring characters, though some faces did appear more than once, like the Nerdy Kid
item.content:encoded: One of the biggest differences between The Far Side and most other comic strips is that The Far Side doesn’t have a recurring cast of characters. Charles Schulz’s Peanuts, for example, had Charlie Brown, Linus, Lucy, Snoopy, and the rest of the gang, while Jim Davis’ Garfield has Garfield, Odie, Jon, and a handful of other recurring characters. But Gary Larson’s The Far Side, with its non-sequitur, single-panel jokes, didn’t have regular characters, or at least not really.

item.title: 5 Near-Perfect Psychological Thriller Movies Streaming for Free
item.dc:creator: Debopriyaa Dutta
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: streaming clickbait headline] These tense genre picks are well worth your time.
item.content:encoded: Psychological thrillers trigger a fight-or-flight response within a controlled environment and entertain us at the same time. Interpersonal relationships become the source of anxiety, as there’s more at stake than someone’s physical safety — their very sanity is on the line. The novelty of great psychological thrillers like Rear Window (1954), Memento (2000), or Mulholland Drive (2001) does not wear off after a first watch. There’s more to glean than suspense or twist, as catharsis is an integral part of the experience. Unfortunately, all those movies are locked up behind various streaming service subscriptions (if they're available to stream at all).

item.title: 23 Years Later, Spike's Best 'Buffy' Quote Is Still One of the Best Lines in TV History
item.dc:creator: Jake Kleinman
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old TV show, not new content.] Spike's best quote sums up his arc as one of the main characters in Buffy the Vampire Slayer.
item.content:encoded: Buffy’s writers gave Spike some of the show’s sharpest one-liners — who could forget “Out. For. A. Walk. Bitch.”? But his best line comes in the series finale, “Chosen.” It’s the natural culmination of a character pulled between heroism and selfishness for most of his life, and it captures the complicated truth of his relationship with Buffy.

item.title: 61 Years Later, Paul's Best Dune Line Is Still the Coldest Quote in Sci-Fi History
item.dc:creator: Debopriyaa Dutta
item.description: [Filtered: Book quote retrospective, not games or horror content.] This brilliant quote from Frank Herbert's Dune reveals an unsavory truth.
item.content:encoded: That said, the phenomenal success of Denis Villeneuve’s Dune movies proves that the impossible is always within reach. So far, Villeneuve’s adaptation has captured the sheer scale of the books and also made some meaningful changes to the source material. This version of Paul Atreides (Timothée Chalamet) begins his journey with a hesitant vulnerability that feels more intense than in the books. This is also why his turn as a self-proclaimed messiah feels more ominous and devastating in Dune: Part Two.
